GetCity is GET /cities/{cityId}:

curl "$WEATHER_ENDPOINT"'/cities/c-0a1b2c3d?at=2026-01-02T03%3A04%3A05Z' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $WEATHER_TOKEN" \
  -H 'Crucible-Version: 2026-10-01'

It answers 200 with a JSON body:

{
  "city": {
    "id": "c-0a1b2c3d",
    "name": "Lisbon"
  },
  "forecast": {
    "clear": {
      "highC": 21
    }
  }
}

Each of the API's simple types is written in JSON like this:

API typeJSON
stringa string
32-bit integer (integer)a whole number
64-bit integer (long)a whole number, every digit written
64-bit float (double)a number
timestampa string in RFC 3339: "2026-01-31T09:30:00Z", unless the member names another format
any JSON value (document)any JSON value
bytes (blob)a string of base64

A structure is an object with a member for each of its members, a list is an array, a map is an object, an enum is its value as a string, and a union is an object with exactly one member, named for the variant it holds. Leave an optional member out to send nothing for it. In a path, a query string or a header, a value is written as text. A parser that reads every JSON number as a double (JavaScript's JSON.parse) rounds a whole number past 2^53: read a response with one that keeps every digit where a value can be that large.

sections.html: One operation returns its results in pages. A response carries the next page's token (nextToken in the JSON body) when another page follows: send it as the query parameter nextToken in the next request, with the other parameters unchanged, until a response has none. A page size is asked for with the query parameter maxResults. A token is opaque: do not read or build one, and stop if the service returns the same token twice.

sections.html:
A request that fails answers with a 4xx or 5xx status. The X-Crucible-Error header names the error, and an error's JSON body repeats the name in __type, beside the error's members:

HTTP/1.1 409
Content-Type: application/json
X-Crucible-Error: ConflictError

{
  "__type": "ConflictError",
  "message": "Lisbon already exists"
}

Tell errors apart by that name, not by the message. Each operation's page lists the errors it returns, with the status of each and whether a retry can succeed. Every response carries the request's ID in x-request-id: quote it when you report a failure.

#include "weather/client.h"

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* The client asks for the token on every attempt, so a refreshed one is used. */
static weather_status read_token(void *user, const weather_scope *scope, weather_arena *arena,
    bool *present, weather_string *token, weather_error *error) {
    const char *value = getenv("WEATHER_TOKEN");
    (void)user;
    (void)scope;
    (void)arena;
    (void)error;
    *present = value != NULL;
    *token = weather_string_view(value);
    return weather_ok;
}

int main(void) {
    weather_error error = {0};
    weather_client_config config = weather_client_defaults();
    config.endpoint = weather_string_view(getenv("WEATHER_ENDPOINT"));
    config.token = read_token;
    weather_client *client = NULL;
    if (weather_client_new(&config, &client, &error) != weather_ok) {
        fprintf(stderr, "weather_client_new: %s\n", error.message);
        return 1;
    }
    /* Call operations with the client, then free it. */
    weather_client_free(client);
    return 0;
}

config.token is the bearer token callback: the client calls it on every attempt (with config.token_user), so a refreshed token is used, and sends no token when it sets *present to false. The client copies config's strings; free it with weather_client_free after its calls and iterators finish. config.endpoint is the service's base URL. The client sends Authorization: Bearer <token> and Crucible-Version: 2026-10-01 on every request.

#include "weather/client.h"

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* The client asks for the token on every attempt, so a refreshed one is used. */
static weather_status read_token(void *user, const weather_scope *scope, weather_arena *arena,
    bool *present, weather_string *token, weather_error *error) {
    const char *value = getenv("WEATHER_TOKEN");
    (void)user;
    (void)scope;
    (void)arena;
    (void)error;
    *present = value != NULL;
    *token = weather_string_view(value);
    return weather_ok;
}

int main(void) {
    weather_error error = {0};
    /* The client sends Authorization: Bearer <token> and Crucible-Version: 2026-10-01 on every request. */
    weather_client_config config = weather_client_defaults();
    config.endpoint = weather_string_view(getenv("WEATHER_ENDPOINT"));
    config.token = read_token;
    weather_client *client = NULL;
    if (weather_client_new(&config, &client, &error) != weather_ok) {
        fprintf(stderr, "weather_client_new: %s\n", error.message);
        return 1;
    }

    /* Values from the model's example "Read a city". */
    weather_models_get_city_input input = {0};
    weather_models_get_city_input_set_city_id(&input, weather_string_view("c-0a1b2c3d"));
    weather_models_get_city_input_set_at(&input, (weather_timestamp){1767323045, 0} /* 2026-01-02T03:04:05Z */);

    weather_operations_get_city_result result = {0};
    weather_status status = weather_operations_get_city(client, &input, NULL, NULL, &result, &error);
    if (status == weather_ok) {
        weather_string text = {0};
        if (weather_models_city_summary_debug(result.base.arena, weather_models_get_city_output_get_city(result.value), &text, &error) == weather_ok) printf("city: %.*s\n", (int)text.length, text.data);
        if (weather_models_get_city_output_has_forecast(result.value) && weather_models_forecast_debug(result.base.arena, weather_models_get_city_output_get_forecast(result.value), &text, &error) == weather_ok) printf("forecast: %.*s\n", (int)text.length, text.data);
        if (weather_models_get_city_output_has_request_id(result.value)) {
            text = weather_models_get_city_output_get_request_id(result.value);
            printf("requestId: %.*s\n", (int)text.length, text.data);
        }
    } else if (weather_error_as_not_found_error(&result.base) != NULL) {
        weather_string text = {0};
        const weather_models_not_found_error *failure = weather_error_as_not_found_error(&result.base);
        fprintf(stderr, "NotFoundError (HTTP %d)\n", result.base.response.status);
        text = weather_models_not_found_error_get_message(failure);
        fprintf(stderr, "message: %.*s\n", (int)text.length, text.data);
    } else {
        fprintf(stderr, "GetCity failed: %s\n", error.message);
    }
    weather_operations_get_city_result_free(&result);
    weather_client_free(client);
    return status == weather_ok ? 0 : 1;
}

A paginated operation also has <operation>_pages_new (weather_operations_list_cities_pages_new), which takes the input and returns a weather_pages iterator, and <operation>_pages_next, which fills one page's result and sets has_page to false after the last one. Free each page's result with <operation>_result_free and the iterator with weather_pages_free.

#include "weather/client.h"

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

/* The client asks for the token on every attempt, so a refreshed one is used. */
static weather_status read_token(void *user, const weather_scope *scope, weather_arena *arena,
    bool *present, weather_string *token, weather_error *error) {
    const char *value = getenv("WEATHER_TOKEN");
    (void)user;
    (void)scope;
    (void)arena;
    (void)error;
    *present = value != NULL;
    *token = weather_string_view(value);
    return weather_ok;
}

int main(void) {
    weather_error error = {0};
    /* The client sends Authorization: Bearer <token> and Crucible-Version: 2026-10-01 on every request. */
    weather_client_config config = weather_client_defaults();
    config.endpoint = weather_string_view(getenv("WEATHER_ENDPOINT"));
    config.token = read_token;
    weather_client *client = NULL;
    if (weather_client_new(&config, &client, &error) != weather_ok) {
        fprintf(stderr, "weather_client_new: %s\n", error.message);
        return 1;
    }

    /* Values from the model's example "List the first page". */
    weather_string const input_tags_items[] = {
        weather_string_view("coastal"),
        weather_string_view("capital"),
    };
    weather_models_tags input_tags = {2, input_tags_items};
    weather_models_list_cities_input input = {0};
    weather_models_list_cities_input_set_max_results(&input, 2);
    weather_models_list_cities_input_set_tags(&input, &input_tags);

    /* Each page is one response; the iterator sends `nextToken` for the next. */
    weather_pages *pages = NULL;
    weather_status status = weather_operations_list_cities_pages_new(client, &input, NULL, NULL, &pages, &error);
    bool has_page = status == weather_ok;
    while (has_page) {
        weather_operations_list_cities_result page = {0};
        status = weather_operations_list_cities_pages_next(pages, &has_page, &page, &error);
        if (status == weather_ok && has_page) {
            weather_string text = {0};
            if (weather_models_city_summaries_debug(page.base.arena, weather_models_list_cities_output_get_cities(page.value), &text, &error) == weather_ok) printf("cities: %.*s\n", (int)text.length, text.data);
        }
        weather_operations_list_cities_result_free(&page);
        if (status != weather_ok) break;
    }
    if (status != weather_ok) fprintf(stderr, "ListCities failed: %s\n", error.message);
    weather_pages_free(pages);
    weather_client_free(client);
    return status == weather_ok ? 0 : 1;
}

import (

		Endpoint: os.Getenv("WEATHER_ENDPOINT"),

sections.html:
A paginated operation also has a <Operation>Pages method (client.ListCitiesPages(input)) returning a paginator: call NextPage(ctx) while HasMorePages() is true. Each page is one response; a repeated token stops it with an error. A paginator is for one goroutine at a time. Every method takes a context.Context first; an operation without input takes weather.Unit{}.

package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"log"
	"os"

	"example.com/weather"
)

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	// The client sends Authorization: Bearer <token> and Crucible-Version: 2026-10-01 on every request.
	client, err := weather.NewWeatherClient(weather.Config{
		Endpoint: os.Getenv("WEATHER_ENDPOINT"),
		Token:    func(context.Context) (string, error) { return os.Getenv("WEATHER_TOKEN"), nil },
	})
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}

	// Values from the model's example "List the first page".
	input := &weather.ListCitiesInput{
		MaxResults: weather.Some(int32(2)),
		Tags:       weather.Some(weather.Tags{"coastal", "capital"}),
	}

	// Each page is one response; the paginator sends `nextToken` for the next.
	pages, err := client.ListCitiesPages(input)
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	for pages.HasMorePages() {
		page, err := pages.NextPage(ctx)
		if err != nil {
			log.Fatal(err)
		}
		fmt.Println(page.Cities)
	}
}

A paginated operation also has a <operation>Pages method returning Pages<Output>, an AsyncSequence of pages (for try await page in try client.listCitiesPages(input)): each page is one response, each step makes one call, and it stops when the response carries no next token.

import Foundation
import Weather

// The client sends Authorization: Bearer <token> and Crucible-Version: 2026-10-01 on every request.
let client = try WeatherClient(ClientConfig(
    endpoint: ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["WEATHER_ENDPOINT"],
    token: { ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["WEATHER_TOKEN"] }
))

// Values from the model's example "List the first page".
let input = ListCitiesInput(
    maxResults: 2,
    tags: [
        "coastal",
        "capital",
    ]
)

// Each page is one response; the paginator sends `nextToken` for the next.
for try await page in try client.listCitiesPages(input) {
    print(page.cities)
}
client.close()

sections.html: Calls are retried with backoff when a retry is safe: a modelled throttling error is retried for any operation; transport failures, HTTP 500, 502, 503 and 504 and other retryable modelled errors only for operations that are read-only, idempotent or carry an idempotency token. For operations that declare an idempotency token, an unset token is generated once per call and reused on every attempt; set it yourself to replay one logical request across calls. These operations fill a token: createCity (clientToken). Set maxAttempts in ClientConfig to change the attempt limit (3, the first included; 1 turns retries off), and baseDelay and maxDelay for the backoff.

import { WeatherClient } from "@example/weather";
import type * as models from "@example/weather";

const client = new WeatherClient({ token: process.env.WEATHER_TOKEN });

token is the bearer token: a string, or a function returning one or a promise of one, called for every attempt so a refreshed token is used. The client sends Authorization: Bearer <token> and Crucible-Version: 2026-10-01 on every request, and x-amz-content-sha256 (content-sha256) on every POST, PUT and PATCH (the empty body's digest when there is none) and any other request with a body.

sections.html:
getCity calls GetCity. Every operation has a method like it.

import { NotFoundError, WeatherClient } from "@example/weather";
import type * as models from "@example/weather";

// The client sends Authorization: Bearer <token> and Crucible-Version: 2026-10-01 on every request, and x-amz-content-sha256 (content-sha256) on every POST, PUT and PATCH (the empty body's digest when there is none) and any other request with a body.
const client = new WeatherClient({ token: process.env.WEATHER_TOKEN });

// Values from the model's example "Read a city".
const input: models.GetCityInput = {
  cityId: "c-0a1b2c3d",
  at: new Date("2026-01-02T03:04:05Z"),
};

try {
  const output = await client.getCity(input);
  console.log(output.city);
  console.log(output.forecast);
  console.log(output.requestId);
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof NotFoundError) {
    console.error(`NotFoundError (HTTP ${error.$metadata.status}):`, error.message);
  } else {
    throw error;
  }
}

sections.html:
Every value is typed. The API's simple types are these in TypeScript:

API typeTypeScript
stringstring
32-bit integer (integer)number
64-bit integer (long)bigint
64-bit float (double)number
timestampDate
any JSON value (document)Document
bytes (blob)Uint8Array

Each named API type is exported under its own name, and a simple one is an alias of the type above (an API string named Id is type Id = string). A list is T[], a map Record<string, V>, and an enum a const object with a type of its values. An optional member is an optional property: leave it out, and pass null only where the API accepts it. A bigint holds the integers a number cannot hold exactly; stringifyJson, exported from the package, serializes values that contain one, which JSON.stringify refuses. A timestamp read from a response is a PreciseDate, a Date that keeps the nanoseconds.

A paginated operation also has a paginate<Operation> method returning an async iterator of pages (for await (const page of client.paginateListCities(input))): each page is one response, and it stops when the response carries no next token.

import { WeatherClient } from "@example/weather";
import type * as models from "@example/weather";

// The client sends Authorization: Bearer <token> and Crucible-Version: 2026-10-01 on every request, and x-amz-content-sha256 (content-sha256) on every POST, PUT and PATCH (the empty body's digest when there is none) and any other request with a body.
const client = new WeatherClient({ token: process.env.WEATHER_TOKEN });

// Values from the model's example "List the first page".
const input: models.ListCitiesInput = {
  maxResults: 2,
  tags: [
    "coastal",
    "capital",
  ],
};

// Each page is one response; the paginator sends `nextToken` for the next.
for await (const page of client.paginateListCities(input)) {

}
